Which ABC sitcom ran for 11 seasons from 1974 to 1984, making it one of the network's longest-running primetime shows?
questions.explanation: Happy Days aired on ABC from 1974 to 1984, spanning 11 seasons and becoming one of the network's longest-running primetime series. The show made a cultural icon out of Arthur "The Fonz" Fonzarelli, played by Henry Winkler, and even gave rise to the phrase "jumping the shark" from one of its later episodes.

questions.question: Which beloved British sitcom character was created by Rowan Atkinson and Richard Curtis?
questions.explanation: Mr. Bean is a classic British sitcom that first aired in 1990, starring Rowan Atkinson as the bumbling, largely silent title character. The show was co-created by Atkinson and screenwriter Richard Curtis, who later became famous for romantic comedies like Four Weddings and a Funeral. Mr. Bean's slapstick humor has made it one of the most internationally recognized British TV shows ever made.

questions.question: Which Starfleet science officer is the central protagonist of Star Trek: Discovery?
questions.explanation: Michael Burnham, played by Sonequa Martin-Green, is the lead character of Star Trek: Discovery, the first Trek series to center on a non-captain protagonist. The show follows her journey through the Federation-Klingon War of 2256 and beyond.

questions.question: PEN15, the Hulu comedy series in which two of its three creators star as fictionalized versions of their middle-school selves, was co-created by Sam Zvibleman and which actress?
questions.explanation: PEN15 was created by Maya Erskine, Anna Konkle, and Sam Zvibleman, with Erskine and Konkle also starring as adult women playing 13-year-old versions of themselves. The show ran on Hulu from 2019 to 2021 and was praised for its unflinching, cringe-comedy portrayal of middle school life. Specifying Zvibleman (the lesser-known, non-acting co-creator) as the anchor clue makes this a genuine deep cut.
